records.content: Australia uses AUD. Cards are widely accepted, ATMs are readily available, and some merchants apply surcharges; travellers cheques are less accepted. AUSTRAC requires declaration of cash and covered bearer instruments totaling AUD 10,000 equivalent or more when crossing the border.
records.notes: Payment access is based on official guidance. Individual card compatibility, fees and current route-specific customs requirements require checking with the provider/authority.

records.title: Canada: currency and payments
records.content: Canada uses the Canadian dollar. Foreign cards can withdraw cash from ABMs, and most airports have exchange offices. Currency and covered monetary instruments totaling CAD 10,000 equivalent or more must be reported when entering or leaving.
records.notes: Payment access is based on official guidance. Individual card compatibility, fees and current route-specific customs requirements require checking with the provider/authority.

records.title: Spain: currency and payments
records.content: Spain uses euros. ATMs and Visa/Mastercard acceptance are widespread; some merchants set card minimums. Currency/covered instruments of EUR 10,000 equivalent or more must be declared when crossing the EU external border. Check customs requirements for your route.
records.notes: Payment access is based on official guidance. Individual card compatibility, fees and current route-specific customs requirements require checking with the provider/authority.

records.title: United Kingdom: currency and payments
records.content: The UK uses sterling (GBP). Cards/contactless are common; small businesses may require cash. ATMs may charge withdrawal/conversion fees. Cash declarations differ: GBP 10,000 or more for Great Britain/non-UK journeys; EUR 10,000 or more for Northern Ireland/non-EU journeys and arrival from Great Britain. Family/group totals count; check the route-specific rules.
records.notes: Payment access is based on official guidance. Individual card compatibility, fees and current route-specific customs requirements require checking with the provider/authority.

records.title: Norway: currency and payments
records.content: Norway uses the krone (NOK). Almost all establishments accept card or phone payments. Post offices and some grocery stores reject foreign credit cards but accept debit cards. Canada advises a customs declaration for NOK 25,000 equivalent or more when entering or leaving, including cash and covered convertible instruments. Verify current customs requirements.
records.notes: Payment access is based on official guidance. Individual card compatibility, fees and current route-specific customs requirements require checking with the provider/authority.

records.title: United States: currency and payments
records.content: The USA uses USD. Canadian cash/personal cheques are not widely accepted; most banking transactions require a US account. Currency and covered instruments above USD 10,000 must be declared when crossing the border. Check bank/card arrangements and customs requirements before travel.
records.notes: Payment access is based on official guidance. Individual card compatibility, fees and current route-specific customs requirements require checking with the provider/authority.

records.title: Congo Republic: security baseline
records.content: FCDO reports opportunistic crime targeting foreigners in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire and vehicle robberies outside cities. Avoid isolated beaches and walking after dark; use main roads in daylight with vehicle doors locked. Protests may become violent. FCDO advises against all travel within 50km of the CAR border in Likouala. Pool districts retain a risk of sudden clashes despite the 2017 ceasefire.
records.notes: FCDO is the sole authority behind this baseline. Regional restrictions and local conditions may change rapidly; this summary does not establish a safe route or verify conditions on the ground.

records.title: Côte d’Ivoire: security baseline
records.content: Terrorist attacks are possible, including in Abidjan. Armed robbery affects homes and streets; use secure accommodation and pre-arranged taxis, avoiding night walking/public transport. Protests may become violent and block roads; avoid gatherings. FCDO advises against all travel within 40km of Mali/Burkina Faso, northern Zanzan/Savanes and Comoé National Park; all but essential travel within 20km of Liberia because of militia clashes.
records.notes: FCDO is the sole authority behind this baseline. Regional restrictions and local conditions may change rapidly; this summary does not establish a safe route or verify conditions on the ground.

records.title: Gabon: security baseline
records.content: Protests can rapidly become violent; avoid gatherings and military activity and monitor local restrictions. Robbery and armed assault affect visitors; isolated Libreville beaches are especially risky after dark. Use licensed taxis booked for your exclusive use because assaults occur in shared taxis. Carjacking occurs in Libreville; keep vehicles secured and use main routes.
records.notes: FCDO is the sole authority behind this baseline. Regional restrictions and local conditions may change rapidly; this summary does not establish a safe route or verify conditions on the ground.

records.title: Equatorial Guinea: security baseline
records.content: FCDO describes a generally calm political situation but warns security forces react quickly to protests. Malabo and Bata have robbery and carjacking risks, especially isolated areas after dark. Use hotel-arranged taxis and avoid unknown passengers. Expect frequent identity checks and roadblocks; carry a passport or copy and remain non-confrontational. Commercial disputes can lead to detention or blocked departure.
records.notes: FCDO is the sole authority behind this baseline. Regional restrictions and local conditions may change rapidly; this summary does not establish a safe route or verify conditions on the ground.

records.title: Guyana: security baseline
records.content: Violent crime is significant and police capacity limited, especially at night in Georgetown. Stabroek, Tiger Bay, Albouystown and Sophia require particular caution. Pre-book licensed airport transfers: criminals may follow arrivals. Keep vehicle doors locked and use indoor ATMs. Sudden protests may disrupt travel. Venezuela-border tensions and organised crime around remote borders, including the disputed New River Triangle, require local authority advice before travel.
records.notes: FCDO is the sole authority behind this baseline. Regional restrictions and local conditions may change rapidly; this summary does not establish a safe route or verify conditions on the ground.

records.title: Mauritania: security baseline
records.content: Crime is increasing, including daytime burglaries and knife-point robberies in Nouakchott. Avoid isolated beaches and take particular care in Le Cinquième, Dar Naim and Cité Plage. Avoid spontaneous protests and retain emergency food/water supplies. Terrorist attacks cannot be excluded. FCDO advises against all travel to eastern military zones and within 25km of Mali. Military-zone boundaries change and access requires Mauritanian authorisation. Other northern/eastern regions and Western Sahara border areas carry all-but-essential advice, with route exceptions; border landmines remain. Consult the detailed regional map.
records.notes: FCDO is the sole authority behind this baseline. Regional restrictions and local conditions may change rapidly; this summary does not establish a safe route or verify conditions on the ground.

records.title: Sudan: security baseline
records.content: Conflict creates severe risks including looting, checkpoint extortion, kidnapping, arbitrary detention and communications blackouts. Khartoum has widespread violent crime, with increases elsewhere. Secure doors/windows, avoid displaying valuables and do not resist robbery. FCDO advises against all travel except Hala’ib Triangle and Bir Tawil Trapezoid, where it advises against all but essential travel. Ceasefires have repeatedly failed. British in-person consular help and UK evacuations are unavailable; no departure route is assured safe.
records.notes: FCDO is the sole authority behind this baseline. Regional restrictions and local conditions may change rapidly; this summary does not establish a safe route or verify conditions on the ground.

records.title: Suriname: security baseline
records.content: Protests can become violent and block roads. Paramaribo and surrounding areas experience burglary and armed robbery; avoid quiet places such as Palmentuin at night. Guard belongings in busy shopping areas. Interior travellers have been robbed: use established tour companies. Exercise caution around the disputed Guyana/New River Triangle and French Guiana border areas.
records.notes: FCDO is the sole authority behind this baseline. Regional restrictions and local conditions may change rapidly; this summary does not establish a safe route or verify conditions on the ground.

records.title: South Sudan: security baseline
records.content: FCDO advises against all travel. Conflict may deteriorate rapidly, block routes and close Juba airport. Prepare independent plans to leave or shelter, with documents and essential supplies. Juba has serious crime, especially at night and on public transport; Juba-Nimule road suffers armed attacks. Avoid travel after dark and protests. Aid workers face kidnapping and arbitrary detention. Mines/unexploded weapons affect several states including Equatorias, Jonglei, Lakes, Upper Nile and Warrap; avoid marked areas and suspicious objects.
records.notes: FCDO is the sole authority behind this baseline. Regional restrictions and local conditions may change rapidly; this summary does not establish a safe route or verify conditions on the ground.

records.title: Chad: security baseline
records.content: Terrorist attacks and kidnapping are serious risks, especially Lake Chad and border regions. Avoid gatherings; protests can turn violent. N’Djamena has armed robbery and roads outside it have high carjacking risk even by day. Use pre-arranged secure vehicles, avoid night travel and obtain professional security advice and required permits before leaving the capital. FCDO advises against all travel to Borkou, Ennedi Ouest/Est, Tibesti, western Kanem including Nokou, Lake Chad and within 30km of other borders; all but essential travel elsewhere. Northern border mines, rebels and contested gold sites add risk.
records.notes: FCDO is the sole authority behind this baseline. Regional restrictions and local conditions may change rapidly; this summary does not establish a safe route or verify conditions on the ground.

records.title: Congo Republic: entry requirements for British passport holders
records.content: FCDO guidance for full British-citizen passports travelling from the UK. Passport must cover the stay; obtain a visa before travel. Carry yellow-fever and polio vaccination certificates. Enhanced health screening may apply. Declare restricted or dutiable goods.
records.notes: Nationality, travel purpose, transit route, age and residency can change requirements. This record covers the source’s British-passport scope, not all nationalities. Confirm personal eligibility and current border rules with destination authorities before booking.

records.title: Côte d’Ivoire: entry requirements for British passport holders
records.content: FCDO guidance for full British-citizen passports travelling from the UK. Passport needs six months remaining on arrival. Obtain a visa or approved e-visa before departure; FCDO recommends applying at least ten working days ahead, with approved e-visas collected at Abidjan airport. Carry yellow-fever certification. Travellers from Ebola-affected countries face screening and possible monitoring. Declare foreign currency and restricted/dutiable goods; CFA cash imports are limited.
records.notes: Nationality, travel purpose, transit route, age and residency can change requirements. This record covers the source’s British-passport scope, not all nationalities. Confirm personal eligibility and current border rules with destination authorities before booking.

records.title: Ecuador: entry requirements for British passport holders
records.content: FCDO guidance for full British-citizen passports travelling from the UK. Passport needs six months remaining on arrival. Tourism is visa-free for 90 days per twelve months; extend before expiry. Work/business/study require separate checks. Land/river arrivals from Peru/Colombia need an apostilled Spanish criminal-record certificate or requested SIMIEC check, subject to exemptions. Use official checkpoints, register entry/exit and obtain stamps; onward-travel proof may be requested. Galapagos requires a transit card, accommodation/host evidence, return mainland flight and health insurance; maximum visit 60 days. Check child exit-consent rules for residents/stays over 90 days. Taxable goods or cash of USD 10,000 or more require digital customs filing at least three days before travel; outward cash declaration and tax rules also apply.
records.notes: Nationality, travel purpose, transit route, age and residency can change requirements. This record covers the source’s British-passport scope, not all nationalities. Confirm personal eligibility and current border rules with destination authorities before booking.

records.title: Gabon: entry requirements for British passport holders
records.content: FCDO guidance for full British-citizen passports travelling from the UK. Passport needs six months remaining on arrival. Apply for a visa before departure; business travellers need a local invitation explaining the trip, tourists accommodation confirmation. Carry yellow-fever vaccination certification. Declare restricted or dutiable goods.
records.notes: Nationality, travel purpose, transit route, age and residency can change requirements. This record covers the source’s British-passport scope, not all nationalities. Confirm personal eligibility and current border rules with destination authorities before booking.

records.title: Equatorial Guinea: entry requirements for British passport holders
records.content: FCDO guidance for full British-citizen passports travelling from the UK. Passport needs six months remaining on arrival. A visa is required; print the e-visa letter or arrange an embassy visa. Ensure the visa and entry stamp are issued to avoid detention/delays. Short visas cover 90 days; longer stays require local procedures/residence permits. Carry yellow-fever certification; health questionnaires may apply. Declare restricted/dutiable goods.
records.notes: Nationality, travel purpose, transit route, age and residency can change requirements. This record covers the source’s British-passport scope, not all nationalities. Confirm personal eligibility and current border rules with destination authorities before booking.

records.title: Guyana: entry requirements for British passport holders
records.content: FCDO guidance for full British-citizen passports travelling from the UK. Passport needs six months remaining on arrival. Visits are normally visa-free for 30 days; apply for extensions and check separate work/student requirements. Overstaying can cause arrest, fines and deportation. Yellow-fever certification is needed when arriving from a transmission-risk country. Declare restricted or dutiable goods.
records.notes: Nationality, travel purpose, transit route, age and residency can change requirements. This record covers the source’s British-passport scope, not all nationalities. Confirm personal eligibility and current border rules with destination authorities before booking.

records.title: Mauritania: entry requirements for British passport holders
records.content: FCDO guidance for full British-citizen passports travelling from the UK. Passport needs six months remaining on arrival. Apply online for an e-visa before travel; visas on arrival are unavailable. Bring a printed e-visa and exact fee in euros or US dollars for payment on arrival; no change or receipt is provided. Yellow-fever certification is required from transmission-risk countries. Declare restricted or dutiable goods.
records.notes: Nationality, travel purpose, transit route, age and residency can change requirements. This record covers the source’s British-passport scope, not all nationalities. Confirm personal eligibility and current border rules with destination authorities before booking.

records.title: Sudan: entry requirements for British passport holders
records.content: FCDO guidance for full British-citizen passports travelling from the UK. Passport needs six months remaining on arrival and a visa. Single-entry holders require an exit visa, inconsistently enforced. Permits are needed beyond Red Sea State; other state procedures vary. Israeli passport stamps/visas prevent entry. Carry yellow-fever certification; register with the Aliens Department within three days. Children need paternal consent or applicable custody documentation; confirm embassy procedures. Declare restricted/dutiable goods. Entry documents do not overcome conflict-related travel warnings.
records.notes: Nationality, travel purpose, transit route, age and residency can change requirements. This record covers the source’s British-passport scope, not all nationalities. Confirm personal eligibility and current border rules with destination authorities before booking.

records.title: Suriname: entry requirements for British passport holders
records.content: FCDO guidance for full British-citizen passports travelling from the UK. Passport needs six months remaining on arrival. Tourism is visa-free for up to 90 days with an entry fee paid before travel. Work/study/business or longer stays require separate permissions. Complete the Immigration and Customs Form within the three-day window before both arrival and departure. Yellow-fever certification is required from transmission-risk countries. Declare restricted/dutiable goods.
records.notes: Nationality, travel purpose, transit route, age and residency can change requirements. This record covers the source’s British-passport scope, not all nationalities. Confirm personal eligibility and current border rules with destination authorities before booking.

records.title: South Sudan: entry requirements for British passport holders
records.content: FCDO guidance for full British-citizen passports travelling from the UK. Passport needs six months remaining on arrival and two blank pages. Obtain a visa for entry or transit and appropriate work permits. Register with police for stays of at least five days. Carry yellow-fever certification; document problems can cause detention or expulsion. Health screening/declarations may apply, especially border travel from DRC/Uganda. Declare restricted/dutiable goods. FCDO advises against all travel.
records.notes: Nationality, travel purpose, transit route, age and residency can change requirements. This record covers the source’s British-passport scope, not all nationalities. Confirm personal eligibility and current border rules with destination authorities before booking.

records.title: Chad: entry requirements for British passport holders
records.content: FCDO guidance for full British-citizen passports travelling from the UK. Passport needs six months remaining on arrival and a visa arranged through a Chadian embassy. Register with police for stays exceeding 72 hours and bring a passport photograph. Yellow-fever certification is required from transmission-risk countries. Declare restricted or dutiable goods.
records.notes: Nationality, travel purpose, transit route, age and residency can change requirements. This record covers the source’s British-passport scope, not all nationalities. Confirm personal eligibility and current border rules with destination authorities before booking.

records.title: Bahrain: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Emergency treatment is charged; arrange insurance and accessible funds for care and repatriation. Carry a doctor’s note for prescribed medicines and check whether prior import approval is required. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel. NaTHNaC advises keeping routine vaccines current, with hepatitis A/B and typhoid vaccination assessed by individual risk. It identifies presumed MERS risk: avoid camel contact and raw camel products; practise food/water hygiene. Yellow-fever certification depends on origin/transit and age, despite no local transmission risk.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Congo Republic: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Facilities are limited, especially rurally; treatment beyond basic care is likely to require evacuation. Arrange air-ambulance insurance, carry local provider contacts and sufficient labelled medication with prescriptions. Seek prompt medical advice for illness during or after travel. Listed risks include yellow fever, schistosomiasis, malaria, dengue and mpox. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Côte d’Ivoire: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Abidjan has reasonable but costly care; emergency facilities are concentrated in a few hospitals and provision elsewhere is basic. Serious treatment may require evacuation; arrange insurance and accessible funds. FCDO lists Zika, malaria, dengue, yellow fever and Ebola among health risks requiring pre-travel assessment. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Ecuador: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Public care is free to foreigners but faces appointment and medicine shortages. Private hospitals can require credit-card guarantees; specialist access is limited outside major cities. Galapagos facilities are limited: include air evacuation in insurance. Oropouche, altitude illness and strong UV exposure are risks. Drink boiled, filtered or bottled water and avoid ice. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Gabon: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Medical facilities are limited, particularly rurally; emergency assistance and phone connections may be unreliable. Arrange treatment/repatriation cover and available funds. Yellow fever, malaria, dengue and Zika are listed risks. Take precautions against HIV exposure. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Equatorial Guinea: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: FCDO describes generally poor medical facilities, with La Paz hospital in Malabo an exception; emergency capacity is extremely limited and serious treatment likely requires evacuation. Arrange insurance and funds; Malabo/Bata pharmacies stock basic medicines. Listed risks include malaria, dengue, schistosomiasis, Zika and altitude illness. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Guyana: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Medical facilities are very limited even in Georgetown and extremely limited remotely. Arrange evacuation for serious/invasive care where possible, with insurance and available funds. Risks include yellow fever, dengue, Zika, Oropouche and malaria in the interior; altitude illness can occur. Take precautions against HIV exposure. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Israel: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Medical care is charged and can be expensive; hospitals insist on payment and may seek legal restrictions on departure over unpaid bills. Arrange insurance and accessible funds for treatment and repatriation. Confirm medication rules and the local facilities needed for existing conditions. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel. NaTHNaC advises current routine immunisations, including tetanus. Stays of four weeks or longer may require a polio ICVP on exit documenting vaccination four weeks to twelve months before departure; confirm with a clinician.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Mauritania: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Facilities are extremely limited, especially outside Nouakchott/Nouadhibou; poor communications complicate emergencies. Clinics may demand euros/dollars and reject foreign insurance cards. Carry adequate prescription supplies because medicines can be unavailable or counterfeit; arrange insurance and funds. Risks listed include dengue, yellow fever, biting insects and Rift Valley fever. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Sudan: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Conflict has disabled many health services; emergency response is often unavailable and treatment beyond basic care may require evacuation. Poor immunisation and clean-water access increase disease risk, especially in conflict areas and camps. Cholera, malaria, yellow fever, dengue, chikungunya and measles are concerns. Arrange insurance and assess whether necessary care can actually be accessed. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Suriname: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Medical facilities are severely limited. Some require advance payment rather than insurer settlement: keep funds and treatment/repatriation insurance available. Yellow fever, Zika, dengue and schistosomiasis are listed health risks. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: South Sudan: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Facilities are extremely limited nationwide; many conditions require evacuation, commonly to Nairobi/Kampala, and rain can delay flights. Arrange cover and funds. No public emergency medical number exists; limited private ambulances require prior clinic registration. Malaria risk is high; cholera, yellow fever and mpox are concerns. Eastern Equatoria mountain routes also have altitude risk. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Syria: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Conflict has damaged or closed many facilities; basic medicines and supplies are scarce and emergency services may not respond. Infectious-disease outbreaks recur, particularly rurally. FCDO lists cholera, malaria and altitude illness among risks to assess. Confirm access to needed care and insurance for treatment/evacuation; FCDO advises against all travel. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Chad: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Facilities are poor; even N’Djamena hospitals are stretched and may experience strikes. Arrange insurance and funds for treatment/repatriation. Cholera and altitude illness are risks. Use boiled or bottled water and avoid ice; take precautions against HIV exposure. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Yemen: healthcare and health preparation
records.content: Medical facilities are poor, especially outside major towns, and conflict may prevent emergency services responding. Arrange insurance and available funds for treatment/repatriation and assess access to needed care. Risks include malaria, dengue, Middle East respiratory syndrome, schistosomiasis and altitude illness. FCDO advises against all travel. Check current vaccine recommendations at least eight weeks before travel.
records.notes: FCDO guidance records general risks and service limitations, not a clinical assessment or verified hospital availability. Vaccines and preventive medicines depend on itinerary and medical history; consult a travel-health professional. Listed risks do not assert a new outbreak.

records.title: Côte d’Ivoire: laws and local conduct
records.content: Carry your original passport: police may reject copies. Dress modestly at religious sites. Drug offences attract prison/fines. Photography around military/government sites, broadcasters, the Presidency and Abidjan airport is prohibited. Same-sex activity is legal, but partnerships are unrecognised and discrimination protections limited.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: Gabon: laws and local conduct
records.content: Carry passport/visa or certified copies for identity checks. Drug possession can bring severe prison sentences. Photographing government/military buildings or airports is illegal. Same-sex activity is legal, but marriage is unrecognised and discrimination remains a concern without sexual-orientation protections.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: Equatorial Guinea: laws and local conduct
records.content: Carry passport/residence documentation or copies. Drug penalties are severe. Government/military/airport photography is illegal. Public affection may draw hostile attention. Same-sex relationships are legal but marriage and anti-discrimination protections absent.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: Guyana: laws and local conduct
records.content: Drug offences attract lengthy imprisonment and fines: pack your own luggage and refuse others’ packages. Same-sex activity is illegal although rarely prosecuted; public affection may attract negative attention.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: Mauritania: laws and local conduct
records.content: Carry photo-ID copies and dress modestly. During Ramadan avoid daytime public eating, drinking and smoking. Alcohol/pork import and consumption are illegal for everyone. Drugs carry severe penalties. Unauthorised non-Islamic gatherings and proselytising are illegal; blasphemy can carry death. Same-sex activity is criminalised, with death a maximum penalty for men. Obtain permission for photography and avoid government/military sites and security personnel.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: Sudan: laws and local conduct
records.content: Carry photographic ID and dress modestly, respecting Ramadan customs. Alcohol can lead to arrest despite a conditional exemption for non-Muslims. Drug trafficking attracts severe penalties. Avoid photographing government/military sites, utilities, bridges and airports. Same-sex activity and extramarital relationships are illegal. Unmarried unrelated opposite-sex couples cannot share rooms; hotel-room guests are prohibited, so use public meeting areas. Some satellite/radio/recording equipment requires licensing.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: Chad: laws and local conduct
records.content: Carry a certified passport copy; residents also need their residence permit. Respect religious customs and modest dress; avoid daytime public eating/drinking/smoking during Ramadan. Drugs can lead to imprisonment in harsh conditions. Military, government and airport photography needs a permit. Same-sex sexual activity is illegal and carries imprisonment/fines.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: Bahrain: laws and local conduct
records.content: Carry photo ID and dress modestly; respect Ramadan and Shia festivals. Daytime public eating/drinking/smoking during Ramadan can be offences. Public intoxication, offensive gestures and illegal drugs, including residues/CBD, attract penalties. Do not film or redistribute security/military imagery or post insulting political content. Drones require licences. Consensual same-sex activity at age 21+ is not prohibited, but public affection is illegal and reported punishment still occurs.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: Saudi Arabia: laws and local conduct
records.content: Wear loose clothing covering elbows and below knees; women need not wear an abaya or cover hair. Alcohol and drugs attract severe penalties; trafficking can bring death. Public non-Islamic worship/proselytising is prohibited, while private practice is accepted. Sex outside marriage and same-sex relations are illegal, although unmarried tourists may share hotel rooms. Avoid political/religious criticism, including online. Sensitive-site photography is prohibited and media work needs permission. Unpaid debts/disputes can prevent departure; two passports in one name are prohibited.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: Qatar: laws and local conduct
records.content: Carry passport identification; cover shoulders/knees and respect Ramadan fasting customs. Alcohol is limited to licensed arrangements for adults21+; public drinking/intoxication is illegal. Unmarried cohabitation and sex outside marriage, including same-sex activity, are illegal. Public intimacy, insulting gestures, vaping and drug offences can lead to prosecution. Obtain consent before photographing people; drones and journalism need permissions. Religious proselytising and insulting online content can be offences. Unpaid debts may block departure.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: United Arab Emirates: laws and local conduct
records.content: Dress modestly and respect Ramadan customs. Offensive speech/gestures, including online, and public kissing can cause arrest. Alcohol is banned in Sharjah; elsewhere age21+, licensed venues and emirate-specific private-use rules apply. Public intoxication is illegal. Drugs/CBD attract severe penalties, including in transit. Same-sex activity is illegal. Opposite-sex adult relationships are generally lawful but extramarital complaints can trigger prosecution. Sensitive-site photography is restricted; people’s consent and media/equipment permissions may be needed. Unpaid bills can lead to detention. Employers cannot lawfully retain passports.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: Oman: laws and local conduct
records.content: Carry a passport-photo-page copy or resident ID. Dress modestly and respect Ramadan fasting customs. Visitors21+ may drink at licensed venues; public drinking/intoxication and drink-driving are illegal. Vapes cannot be imported or used. Unmarried unrelated opposite-sex couples cannot share accommodation; same-sex activity is illegal. Drugs may attract death penalties. Rude gestures/obscene online posts are offences. Obtain consent for portraits; sensitive-site photography and unlicensed drones are prohibited. Settle debts and traffic fines before departure.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: Kuwait: laws and local conduct
records.content: Carry passport or Kuwaiti resident ID. Dress modestly; avoid daytime public eating/drinking/smoking during Ramadan. Alcohol and same-sex activity are illegal. Unmarried couples cannot share accommodation; hotels may request marriage proof. Insults/obscene gestures and drug offences attract severe penalties, including death for trafficking. Do not photograph government/military/oil infrastructure or people without consent. Clear traffic, phone and utility bills before departure; commercial disputes and unpaid debts can lead to travel bans or detention.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: Iran: laws and local conduct
records.content: Carry passport/visa copies. Dress rules are strictly enforced: women must cover hair and wear long loose covering clothes; men should wear long trousers/sleeves. Avoid daytime public eating/drinking/smoking during Ramadan. Sex outside marriage and same-sex relations can carry death penalties. Alcohol is prohibited except narrow recognised-minority exceptions; drugs carry severe penalties. Photography near sensitive sites or electronic-device use can trigger espionage allegations. Drones/satellite phones need permission. Commercial disputes may block departure.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

records.title: Iraq: laws and local conduct
records.content: Carry passport/residence photo ID and cooperate at checkpoints. Lost passports require police reporting and publication in two local newspapers before exit processing. Respect Ramadan customs; avoid public daytime drinking/smoking and loud music. Alcohol import/manufacture/sale is prohibited; drug trafficking and antiquities smuggling can bring death penalties. Same-sex relationships and promotion of LGBT identities are criminalised; gender-change procedures require court approval. Family-law travel bans and paternal permission may affect children. Journalists need proper paperwork; KRG prohibits sharing drone-launch/target footage.
records.notes: FCDO practical legal/cultural guidance, not a complete statement of local law. Enforcement and local practices can change; confirm permits or individual legal questions with relevant authorities.

sources.notes: Verified 22 Sep 2026 directly from GDACS's own documentation: API quickstart (data.gdacs.org/Documents/2025/GDACS_API_quickstart_v1.pdf), official Terms of Use (gdacs.org/documents/2025/GDACS_Terms_of_use_Mar_25.pdf, March 2025), and live API responses. No authentication required. Endpoints used: https://www.gdacs.org/gdacsapi/api/events/geteventlist/SEARCH (event search, verified live) and https://www.gdacs.org/gdacsapi/api/events/geteventdata (single-event detail — endpoint documented and confirmed reachable, but could not be reliably pinned to a specific requested eventid in this session; treat single-event detail retrieval as REQUIRES VERIFICATION for production use). Licensing is layered, not a single blanket statement: the RSS channel itself is tagged copyright:'public domain' by GDACS; the geteventdata API resource's own acknowledgements metadata states 'Copyright notice: European Union (CC BY 4.0), reuse is allowed, provided appropriate credit to GDACS is given'; other JRC-sourced resources (episode RSS, CAP, KML) state 'Copyright European Union. Syndication allowed, provided the source is acknowledged.' GDACS's own API quickstart doc: 'We only request to acknowledge the source as "Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System, GDACS".' Attribution is required in every variant seen; contentRights recorded as OPEN_LICENCE on that basis. The official Terms of Use (Mar 2025) explicitly states earthquake, tsunami and tropical-cyclone notifications are automatic/algorithmic, not reviewed by human experts before issuance, may contain uncertainties/errors, and 'should not be used for decision making without prior confirmation of their validity' — reflected in every derived SourceObservation's uncertainty field; TI never marks a GDACS-only event as CONFIRMED. Some GDACS API resources (e.g. certain polygon geometry endpoints) are marked accesslevel:Private in the feed's own metadata, so not all GDACS data is uniformly public — only geteventlist/SEARCH and geteventdata were verified accesslevel:Public and used here. jurisdiction intentionally left unset: GDACS is a supranational cooperation framework (UN + EC), not a single national jurisdiction. sourceQualityGrade intentionally left unset (not yet graded), consistent with the 121 FCDO sources and with GDACS's own stated need for further validation. independenceGroupId for every GDACS-derived observation is 'gdacs-ecjrc', deliberately distinct from any FCDO group.

Verified 22 Sep 2026 from ReliefWeb's own official documentation (apidoc.reliefweb.int, including its Swagger/OpenAPI spec) and its Terms of Service page. API v2, base https://api.reliefweb.int/v2, read-only, JSON responses; example endpoint https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=...&limit=2. Every call requires an 'appname' parameter, and per ReliefWeb's own documentation, 'From 1 November 2025, API users will require a pre-approved appname' obtained via a request form with roughly one business day's turnaround — TI does NOT currently hold a pre-approved appname, so automationPermission is recorded as UNKNOWN rather than PERMITTED (unlike GDACS, which explicitly permits anyone/any automated use with no onboarding). Quotas: max 1000 entries per call, max 1000 calls per day. Rights position is layered: the API's own Swagger spec states its metadata/schema is licensed CC0 (Creative Commons Zero – Public Domain); OCHA's general site footer states CC BY 4.0; but ReliefWeb's own Terms of Service explicitly warns that 'Reports, Jobs and Training data available via ReliefWeb API is contributed by information partners and may contain copyrighted material owned by the original source. You should respect the intellectual property rights of the original source.' contentRights is therefore recorded conservatively as FACTUAL_SUMMARY_ONLY — TI extracts only concise factual claims from ReliefWeb items, never reproduces original report text, regardless of the underlying licence of any individual report. ReliefWeb itself is a UN OCHA platform, but the great majority of its content is authored by information partners (UN agencies, NGOs, governments, and commercial analysis firms) rather than by OCHA directly — the originating organisation behind each individual report must be identified and used for independenceGroupId per-observation; ReliefWeb-as-platform is never itself treated as an independent corroborating source alongside its own contributors. A direct live test of the reports endpoint (https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=apidoc&limit=2) was blocked by bot detection in this session — genuinely unresolved; REQUIRES VERIFICATION for any future production integration, alongside the pre-approved-appname gap.
sources.organisation: UN OCHA (ReliefWeb is a UN OCHA humanitarian information platform; individual reports are authored by a wide range of information partners — UN agencies, NGOs, governments, commercial risk-analysis firms — not by OCHA itself unless OCHA is the named source of a specific report)

Escalated to CORROBORATED: UK CAA (an independent regulator, not NATS) and directly-quoted airline statements (Ryanair, easyJet, British Airways) via Aviation Today constitute a reporting chain genuinely distinct from NATS's own statement. events.summary: NATS (UK National Air Traffic Services) reported a technical connectivity fault affecting its Prestwick, Scotland control centre from the morning of 21 Sep 2026, prompting air traffic flow regulations to manage traffic safely while engineers investigated. NATS said the fault was fixed shortly after 11:00 UTC, though delays continued into the afternoon. By late afternoon on 21 Sep, 227 flights had been cancelled, with disruption affecting Manchester, Glasgow, Belfast, Edinburgh, London Gatwick and London City (earlier reporting had also named Northern Ireland, Newcastle, Bristol and Luton). Ryanair said more than 25,000 of its passengers were affected and over 140 of its flights were delayed, and renewed calls for the NATS chief executive to resign; easyJet and British Airways both said the fault raised renewed questions about NATS system resilience. The UK Civil Aviation Authority said affected passengers are unlikely to qualify for cash compensation, as the disruption falls under 'extraordinary circumstances', though airlines must still provide refunds, rebooking or care during delays. NATS said this was unrelated to a separate technical issue earlier in September 2026.

events.summary: A large-scale drone attack struck the Moscow region overnight into 20 Sep 2026, coinciding with the final day of Russia's parliamentary elections. Three people were killed (two initially, a third died later in hospital) and an apartment building in Ramenskoye district was hit, with roughly 400 residents evacuated. Drones reached the grounds of the Moscow Oil Refinery (Gazprom-MNPZ, Kapotnya); both of its primary processing units (AVT-6 and the Euro+ combined unit) caught fire, halting all crude processing, with restoration estimated to take several weeks. The refinery, which supplies roughly 40% of Moscow and Moscow Region's fuel, suspended exchange fuel listings from 21 Sep. Rosaviatsia imposed temporary overnight flight restrictions at Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo, Vnukovo and Zhukovsky airports, lifted the following morning; more than 400 flights were delayed and dozens cancelled across the four airports. Russian officials (Moscow Mayor Sobyanin, Moscow region Governor Vorobyov) attributed the attack to Ukraine; Ukrainian President Zelensky and Ukraine's General Staff subsequently confirmed the strike, describing it as hitting 'one of Russia's key oil industry facilities' in the exercise of Ukraine's 'right to self-defense'.

Zelensky's statement refers to an unnamed 'key oil industry facility' rather than naming the Moscow Oil Refinery specifically; TI infers this is the same facility based on timing and the absence of any other reported refinery strike that night, but this is an inference, not a direct quote match. Casualty figures, refinery damage extent, restoration timeline ('several weeks') and flight-restriction figures are as reported at time of writing and may be revised. This remains a war-casualty security incident kept in DRAFT pending human legal review before any public publication.

events.title: Four Iraqi airports suspend flights to/from Iran after new US aviation sanctions
events.summary: Iraq halted all flights between Iran and four of its international airports — Baghdad (from Wednesday 23 Sep 2026, per a directive from the Iraqi Prime Minister's office), then Najaf, Erbil and Sulaimaniyah (all from Friday 25 Sep 2026) — after Washington's 8 Sep 2026 sanctions on Iran's remaining airlines and its warning that any global company doing business with sanctioned Iranian carriers risks secondary sanctions. Najaf airport director Hussein Muhanna said flights were halted 'following a directive from the prime minister's office to the governor.' Iranian carriers had operated at least 20 daily flights at Najaf alone; only around four non-Iranian flights remained scheduled after the suspension. Travellers between Iran and Iraq — including Shia pilgrims visiting shrine cities in both countries, an estimated 100,000 Iraqi students at Iranian institutions, and hundreds of thousands of Iraqis resident in Iran — now face a mandatory overland journey of at least 12 hours. Ground-service providers (refuelling, baggage handling) complied with the suspension to avoid secondary sanctions exposure. The Iranian Consulate in Najaf publicly objected; the Iraqi federal government made no public statement, reportedly to avoid antagonising pro-Iranian political factions, though Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein has separately called the US sanctions 'unjust and inhumane' and Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's office is seeking a US exemption for humanitarian travel (medical treatment, education, religious visits). The UAE and Qatar have similarly restricted Iran flights to comply with the US measures. Demonstrations backed by Iran-aligned Iraqi political and militia groups have taken place in Baghdad and Basra opposing the suspension, with threats to stage sit-ins at Iraqi airports if normal air traffic does not resume.
events.uncertaintyNotes: The Iraqi federal government has not issued its own public statement on the suspension per the sourcing used here; flight-count and journey-time figures are as reported at time of writing (25-26 Sep 2026) and may change if a US humanitarian exemption is granted. The reporting used (Al Jazeera, itself citing AFP and Reuters) and the US Treasury's own 8 Sep 2026 release are genuinely independent chains, but Treasury's release does not itself name Iraq or the airport suspensions — the causal link rests on the media reporting, not on Treasury's own text. Protest scale and sit-in threats are as reported by Al Jazeera and not independently corroborated by TI beyond that single (wire-sourced) chain.

events.title: US sanctions Iran's remaining airlines, grounding much of Iran's civil aviation fleet (“Operation Economic Outcast”)
events.summary: On 8 Sep 2026 the US Treasury (OFAC) designated 36 targets under Executive Orders 13224 and 13902, including 27 Iranian airlines — among them Mahan Air (previously designated in 2011), Iran Air Tour, Iran Aseman Airlines, Kish Airlines, Qeshm Air, Karun Airlines, Saha Airlines and others — plus nine supporting foreign entities and one individual in the UAE, Turkey, the UK, Malaysia and Kazakhstan accused of helping sanctioned carriers procure aircraft and parts. OFAC also suspended three Iran-related aviation authorisations covering overflights and non-US airlines operating US-origin aircraft into Iran. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said: 'Let this be a warning to anyone doing business with Iran's remaining airlines, all of which we sanctioned today: You are at risk of being cut off from the global financial system.' Treasury states the aviation sector is used by the Iranian regime to move weapons, personnel and illicit cargo, and that OFAC 'will consider aviation safety-related requests on a case-by-case basis.' This is the latest action under 'Operation Economic Outcast' (announced 24 Aug 2026), aimed at severing Iran's remaining international economic and transport links; it directly triggered flight suspensions at four Iraqi airports and restrictions by the UAE and Qatar (see related event iq-ir-flightsuspension-2026-09-23).
events.uncertaintyNotes: Treasury's own release does not itself describe downstream effects in Iraq or elsewhere, nor does it establish a general humanitarian exemption — only a narrow, case-by-case aviation-safety exception. Full extent of Iran's remaining civil aviation capacity after this and prior designations is not independently assessed by TI. RFE/RL reporting corroborates the same target list and Bessent quote without adding independent facts beyond Treasury's own release.

events.title: Coordinated drone strikes hit multiple Russian regions (Ulyanovsk, Perm, Belgorod, Voronezh, Rostov, Samara); casualties and rail/refinery disruption
events.summary: A wave of drone strikes hit at least six Russian regions on 25 Sep 2026, per Russian regional officials (Reuters wire, via ABC News Australia; Reuters states it could not independently verify the reports). Ulyanovsk: 8 people injured; industrial and civilian infrastructure damaged, including a major electronics plant (Governor Alexei Russkikh); TASS separately reports the governor's account via Max messenger of air defences and mobile fire groups 'repelling a massive drone attack' on the city, with unspecified casualties receiving medical assistance. Belgorod: 1 civilian killed and 1 wounded when a drone struck a truck. Perm: 1 man killed in a drone attack on the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery, which temporarily suspended operations (Governor Dmitry Makhonin). Rostov: about 50 drones destroyed overhead; refinery facilities damaged, no reported casualties. Voronezh: 4 injured; 88 drones destroyed overnight; residential buildings, vehicles and industrial facilities damaged. sourceObservations.extractedClaim: Al Jazeera (25 Sep 2026, 18:30 UTC; byline credits Al Jazeera Staff with AFP and Reuters): four Iraqi airports — Baghdad, Najaf, Erbil and Sulaimaniyah — halted flights to/from Iran. Baghdad halted from Wednesday 23 Sep 2026; Najaf halted from Friday 25 Sep 2026 'following a directive from the prime minister's office to the governor' (Najaf airport director Hussein Muhanna); Erbil and Sulaimaniyah followed the same day. Iranian carriers previously operated at least 20 daily flights at Najaf alone; only about four non-Iranian flights remained scheduled afterward. Passengers now face a land journey of at least 12 hours. Ground-service companies complied with the suspension to avoid secondary US sanctions. The Iranian Consulate in Najaf publicly objected ('Najaf international airport...is closed to the largest Shia country in the world?!'). The UAE and Qatar also cancelled or restricted Iran flights. The Iraqi federal government made no public statement, reportedly to avoid antagonising pro-Iranian factions.
sourceObservations.originalTitle: Iraqi airports halt Iranian flights after new US aviation sanctions
sourceObservations.uncertainty: Iraqi federal government made no public statement per this source. Flight-count and journey-time figures as reported at publication and may evolve. Iranian Consulate quote reflects a directly-affected party's public objection, not an independently verified fact.
sourceObservations.notes: Retrieved via direct fetch of aljazeera.com, 27 Sep 2026.

sourceObservations.extractedClaim: Reuters wire, via ABC News Australia (25 Sep 2026; 'Reuters could not independently verify' the officials' reports): coordinated drone strikes hit at least six Russian regions on 25 Sep 2026. Ulyanovsk: 8 injured; industrial and civilian infrastructure damaged including a major electronics plant (Governor Alexei Russkikh). Belgorod: 1 civilian killed, 1 wounded when a drone struck a truck. Perm: 1 man killed in a drone attack on the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery, which temporarily suspended operations (Governor Dmitry Makhonin). sourceObservations.uncertainty: Reuters explicitly states it could not independently verify Russian officials' reports or the attribution to Ukraine.
